question: Why are sound waves classified as mechanical waves?
option_2: They oscillate perpendicular to wave propagation
option_3: They are characterised by the motion of particles in a medium
option_4: They do not require a medium to travel
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are characterised by the motion of particles in a medium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A mechanical wave is a wave that needs a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel, because it moves by making the particles of the medium vibrate and pass on the disturbance to neighbouring particles. (यांत्रिक तरंग — माध्यम के कणों का कंपन)

 

• Sound is produced by a vibrating body, and it propagates as a longitudinal wave in which particles of the medium oscillate back and forth parallel to the direction of propagation, creating alternate regions of compression and rarefaction.

 

• Because sound needs particles of a medium to carry the disturbance, it cannot travel through vacuum — this is why no sound is heard in outer space.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Non-mechanical (electromagnetic) waves, like light, X-rays and radio waves, do not need a medium and can travel through vacuum.

 

• Waves are also classified as transverse (particle motion perpendicular to wave direction, e.g. light, water ripples) or longitudinal (particle motion parallel to wave direction, e.g. sound).

 

• Speed of sound is greatest in solids, less in liquids, and least in gases, since particles are packed closest in solids.

 

NOTE

 

• They cause light oscillations (Option A): Sound waves have nothing to do with light; this describes no real physical property of sound.

 

• They oscillate perpendicular to wave propagation (Option B): This describes a transverse wave, not sound, which is longitudinal.

 

• They do not require a medium to travel (Option D): This is the opposite of the truth — sound absolutely requires a medium, which is exactly why it is called mechanical.

question: Which of the following organs in human females can produce hormones?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ovaries.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ovaries are the primary female reproductive glands (gonads) and act as endocrine glands, secreting the hormones oestrogen and progesterone. (अंडाशय — एस्ट्रोजन एवं प्रोजेस्ट्रोन का स्राव)

 

• Oestrogen is responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics in females (like breast development and a wider pelvis) at puberty, while progesterone prepares and maintains the uterus (endometrium) for pregnancy.

 

• The ovaries also release a mature egg (ovum) once every menstrual cycle, a process called ovulation, making them both a reproductive and a hormone-producing (endocrine) organ.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important endocrine glands in the human body: pituitary (master gland), thyroid (thyroxine), adrenal (adrenaline), pancreas (insulin, via islets of Langerhans), and testes in males (testosterone).

 

• The hypothalamus in the brain controls the pituitary gland, which in turn regulates most other endocrine glands, including the ovaries via FSH and LH.

 

• Menstrual cycle in human females is on average about 28 days, regulated by the cyclic secretion of oestrogen and progesterone.

 

NOTE

 

• Cervix (Option A): The lower, narrow part of the uterus connecting it to the vagina; it is a passage, not a hormone-secreting organ.

 

• Salivary glands (Option B): Exocrine glands that secrete saliva (containing the enzyme salivary amylase) into the mouth; they are not hormone-producing.

 

• Fallopian tubes (Option C): Carry the egg from the ovary to the uterus and are the usual site of fertilisation; they do not secrete hormones.

question: Cells of the meristematic tissue lack vacuoles because:
option_1: Meristematic cells are actively dividing and need a dense cytoplasm
option_3: Meristematic cells are dead and do not need vacuoles
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meristematic cells are actively dividing and need a dense cytoplasm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meristematic tissue consists of small, thin-walled, living cells that divide continuously (at the root tip, shoot tip, etc.) and are packed with a dense cytoplasm to support rapid cell division, so they lack large vacuoles. (विभज्योतक ऊतक — सघन कोशिकाद्रव्य)

 

• These cells have a prominent nucleus relative to cell size and thin cellulose cell walls, both features suited for quick division rather than storage.

 

• As meristematic cells mature into permanent tissue, small vacuoles appear and gradually fuse into one large central vacuole, typical of mature plant cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Meristematic tissue is classified by location: apical (at root/shoot tips, responsible for growth in length), intercalary (at the base of leaves/internodes, e.g. in grasses), and lateral (e.g. vascular cambium, responsible for growth in girth/thickness).

 

• Permanent tissue is formed when meristematic cells lose the ability to divide and become specialised (differentiation) — e.g. parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma.

 

• The large central vacuole in mature plant cells maintains turgor pressure, stores water, nutrients and waste products, and gives the cell rigidity.

 

NOTE

 

• Vacuoles cause cell death (Option B): Factually incorrect — vacuoles support normal cell functions like storage and turgidity, not cell death.

 

• Meristematic cells are dead and do not need vacuoles (Option C): Incorrect — meristematic cells are very much living and actively dividing.

 

• Vacuoles block respiratory enzymes (Option D): There is no such function of vacuoles; this is not a real biological process.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the sequence of events leading to muscle movement?
option_1: Nerve impulse → Muscle protein response → Muscle contraction
option_3: DNA replication → Protein synthesis → Muscle movement
option_4: Blood flow → Protein activation → Nerve impulse → Movement
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nerve impulse → Muscle protein response → Muscle contraction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muscle movement is triggered when a nerve impulse reaches a muscle cell, causing changes in muscle proteins (actin and myosin), which then slide over each other to cause muscle contraction. (तंत्रिका आवेग — पेशी संकुचन)

 

• The nerve impulse causes release of calcium ions inside the muscle cell, which bind to the protein troponin, exposing binding sites on actin so that myosin can attach and pull, shortening the muscle fibre — this is the sliding filament mechanism.

 

• This response is very fast (electrochemical), unlike digestion or DNA replication, which are far slower biochemical processes and are not directly responsible for triggering contraction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muscle tissue is of three types: skeletal (voluntary, striated), smooth (involuntary, unstriated), and cardiac (involuntary, striated).

 

• The chemical energy for muscle contraction comes from ATP; during vigorous exercise when oxygen is insufficient, muscles rely on anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid.

 

• The junction between a nerve cell and a muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction, where the neurotransmitter acetylcholine is released to trigger contraction.

 

NOTE

 

• Digestion → Blood circulation → Movement (Option B): Digestion provides nutrients but does not directly trigger muscle contraction; it is not part of the contraction mechanism.

 

• DNA replication → Protein synthesis → Muscle movement (Option C): DNA replication occurs during cell division, not during the everyday process of muscle movement.

 

• Blood flow → Protein activation → Nerve impulse → Movement (Option D): This reverses the correct order — the nerve impulse comes first and triggers the protein response, not the other way round.

question: What is the formula to calculate the acceleration due to gravity (g), where G is the universal gravitational constant, M is the mass of the Earth, and R is the radius of the Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is g=GM/R2 (i.e. g = GM/R²).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth is given by g = GM/R², where G is the universal gravitational constant, M is the mass of the Earth, and R is the radius of the Earth. (गुरुत्वीय त्वरण — g = GM/R²)

 

• This is derived from Newton's law of gravitation, F = GMm/R², and Newton's second law, F = mg; equating the two and cancelling the test mass m gives g = GM/R².

 

• Near the Earth's surface, this works out to g ≈ 9.8 m/s², since G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², M ≈ 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg, and R ≈ 6.4 × 10⁶ m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• g is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator because the Earth is flattened at the poles (smaller R) and bulges at the equator (larger R), and g is inversely proportional to R².

 

• g decreases both as one goes above the Earth's surface and as one goes below it (towards the centre), becoming zero at the centre.

 

• Weight (W = mg) of a body changes with location (depends on g), but its mass remains constant everywhere.

 

NOTE

 

• g=GM2/R (Option A) and g=GR/M2 (Option C): These place the square incorrectly on M instead of on R; they do not match Newton's derivation.

 

• g=GM/R (Option B): Misses the square on R altogether, which is essential since gravitational force follows an inverse-square law.

question: A concave lens has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the lens. What is the magnification produced by the lens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is +0.33 (approximately +1/3).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For a concave (diverging) lens, using the sign convention (distances measured from the optical centre, distances against incident light negative), focal length f = -15 cm and object distance u = -30 cm. (अवतल लेंस — सदैव आभासी, सीधा, छोटा प्रतिबिंब)

 

• Using the lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/(-15) + 1/(-30) = -2/30 - 1/30 = -3/30 = -1/10, so v = -10 cm.

 

• Magnification m = v/u = (-10)/(-30) = 1/3 ≈ +0.33. A positive magnification less than 1 confirms the image is virtual, erect and diminished — exactly what a concave lens always produces, regardless of object position.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image between the optical centre and the focus, no matter where the real object is placed — this is a key exam fact.

 

• Sign convention (Cartesian): distances measured from the optical centre; distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, against it are negative; heights above the axis are positive.

 

• Power of a lens P = 1/f (in metres); a concave lens always has negative power (in dioptres), while a convex lens has positive power.

 

NOTE

 

• -0.33 (Option A): Wrong sign — a concave lens always gives a positive (erect) magnification, never negative.

 

• +0.66 (Option C) and -0.66 (Option D): Both have the wrong magnitude; only m = v/u = 1/3 ≈ 0.33 satisfies the lens formula for f = -15 cm, u = -30 cm.

question: Which of the following statements best explains kinetic energy?
option_1: It is the energy an object has because it is at rest.
option_2: It is the energy that decreases as the object's speed increases.
option_3: It is the energy stored in an object due to its shape.
option_4: It is the energy an object has because of its motion, and it increases as the object's speed increases.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is the energy an object has because of its motion, and it increases as the object's speed increases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body by virtue of its motion; a stationary body has zero kinetic energy. (गतिज ऊर्जा — गति के कारण ऊर्जा)

 

• It is given by the formula KE = ½ mv², where m is the mass and v is the velocity — since KE is proportional to the square of velocity, it increases rapidly as speed increases.

 

• Examples: a moving car, a flying ball, flowing water, and wind all possess kinetic energy, which is used to do work (e.g. hydro and wind power plants convert kinetic energy of moving water/air into electricity).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Potential energy is energy stored due to position or configuration (e.g. gravitational PE = mgh, or elastic PE stored in a stretched spring/shape).

 

• The Work-Energy theorem states that the work done on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy.

 

• The SI unit of energy is the joule (J), same as the unit of work, since energy is the capacity to do work.

 

NOTE

 

• It is the energy an object has because it is at rest (Option A): This describes zero kinetic energy, the opposite of the concept being tested.

 

• It is the energy that decreases as the object's speed increases (Option B): Incorrect — kinetic energy *increases*, not decreases, with speed.

 

• It is the energy stored in an object due to its shape (Option C): This describes elastic potential energy, not kinetic energy.

question: A satellite is moving in a uniform circular orbit around the Earth. Which of the following statements about its motion is correct?
option_1: The satellite has a constant speed, but its velocity is not constant.
option_2: The satellite has a constant velocity, but its speed is not constant.
option_3: The satellite has a constant velocity and a constant acceleration.
option_4: The satellite has a constant speed and no acceleration.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The satellite has a constant speed, but its velocity is not constant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In uniform circular motion, the speed (magnitude of velocity) stays constant, but the direction of velocity keeps changing continuously as the object moves along the circle, so the velocity (a vector) is not constant. (एकसमान वृत्तीय गति — चाल स्थिर, वेग परिवर्तनशील)

 

• Since velocity changes (in direction, even though not in magnitude), the satellite must have an acceleration, called centripetal acceleration, directed towards the centre of the orbit at every instant, given by a = v²/r.

 

• This centripetal force (here, provided by Earth's gravity) keeps the satellite in its circular path without changing its speed, only redirecting its velocity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uniform circular motion is accelerated motion even though speed is constant, because acceleration depends on the rate of change of the velocity vector, not just its magnitude.

 

• For satellites, the gravitational force F = GMm/r² supplies the necessary centripetal force, so GMm/r² = mv²/r, giving orbital speed v = √(GM/r).

 

• A geostationary satellite orbits at a height of about 35,786 km above the equator with a time period equal to Earth's rotation period (about 24 hours), so it appears stationary relative to a point on Earth.

 

NOTE

 

• The satellite has a constant velocity, but its speed is not constant (Option B): This is exactly backwards — in circular motion it is the speed that stays constant, not the velocity.

 

• The satellite has a constant velocity and a constant acceleration (Option C): If velocity were truly constant (same magnitude and direction), the satellite would move in a straight line, not a circle.

 

• The satellite has a constant speed and no acceleration (Option D): Incorrect — a changing velocity direction always implies acceleration, even at constant speed.

question: Which of the following statements is correct for the magnetic field inside a long, straight, current-carrying solenoid?
option_1: It is the same at all points.
option_2: It decreases as we move towards its end.
option_3: It increases as we move towards its end.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is the same at all points.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Inside a long, straight, current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform — it has the same magnitude and direction at every point well inside the solenoid, parallel to its axis. (परिनालिका — भीतर एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र)

 

• The field lines inside are parallel, straight and equally spaced, which is exactly the pattern seen inside a bar magnet, so a current-carrying solenoid behaves like a bar magnet with one end acting as a north pole and the other as a south pole.

 

• This uniform field is given by B = μ₀nI, where n is the number of turns per unit length and I is the current, provided the solenoid is sufficiently long compared to its diameter (the field near the very ends is somewhat weaker, but is treated as uniform throughout the interior for standard exam purposes).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The magnetic field outside a long solenoid is negligibly weak, essentially zero, unlike outside a bar magnet where field lines curve around from N to S pole.

 

• The right-hand thumb rule (or Maxwell's corkscrew rule) is used to find the direction of the magnetic field due to a current-carrying conductor.

 

• A solenoid with a soft iron core placed inside becomes a powerful electromagnet, used in electric bells, cranes, and relays.

 

NOTE

 

• It decreases as we move towards its end (Option B) and It increases as we move towards its end (Option C): Both wrongly describe a varying field; the field is uniform throughout the interior of a long solenoid.

 

• It is zero (Option D): Incorrect — the field inside a solenoid is strong and uniform, not zero; it is the field *outside* that is nearly zero.

question: How do plant cells respond immediately to a stimulus without specialized proteins like animal muscle cells?
option_2: By breaking down food to release energy instantly
option_3: By changing water content to cause swelling or shrinking
solution_text:
The correct answer is By changing water content to cause swelling or shrinking.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Unlike animal cells, plant cells lack specialised contractile proteins (like actin and myosin), so they respond to a stimulus by changing the amount of water in their cells, causing them to swell (turgid) or shrink (flaccid), which brings about movement. (पादप कोशिका — जल की मात्रा में परिवर्तन से गति)

 

• This water-based movement mechanism relies on osmosis: water moves in or out of the cell through the semi-permeable membrane, changing turgor pressure, which can cause a plant part to bend or move rapidly.

 

• A classic example is the touch-me-not plant (Mimosa pudica), whose leaves fold instantly on touch due to a rapid loss of water (and hence turgor) from cells at the base of the leaflets, called the pulvinus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plant movements caused by external stimuli (touch, light, gravity, chemicals) but not growth-related are called nastic movements (e.g. Mimosa's touch response).

 

• Growth-related directional movements in plants are called tropisms: phototropism (towards light), geotropism/gravitropism (towards/away from gravity), hydrotropism (towards water), and chemotropism (towards a chemical stimulus, e.g. pollen tube growth).

 

• Auxin, a plant hormone, plays a key role in tropic movements by promoting unequal cell growth on different sides of the plant organ.

 

NOTE

 

• By producing immune responses (Option A): Immune responses are unrelated to a plant's mechanism of quick movement.

 

• By breaking down food to release energy instantly (Option B): This describes respiration providing energy generally, not the specific mechanism of rapid movement.

 

• By secreting enzymes only (Option D): Enzyme secretion is involved in digestion/metabolism, not in the water-based movement response to stimuli.

question: What is the main function of leucoplasts in plant cells?
option_4: Storing materials like starch, oils, and proteins
solution_text:
The correct answer is Storing materials like starch, oils, and proteins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Leucoplasts are colourless plastids found in plant cells that are not exposed to sunlight (e.g. in roots, underground stems and seeds), and their main function is the storage of nutrients such as starch, oils and proteins. (श्वेतलवक — स्टार्च, तेल एवं प्रोटीन का भंडारण)

 

• Based on what they store, leucoplasts are classified into three types: amyloplasts (store starch, e.g. in potato tubers), elaioplasts/lipidoplasts (store oils and fats), and aleuroplasts/proteinoplasts (store proteins).

 

• Since they lack pigments, leucoplasts appear white or colourless, distinguishing them from chloroplasts (green, photosynthesis) and chromoplasts (coloured, give colour to flowers/fruits).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plastids are of three main types: chloroplasts (green, contain chlorophyll, site of photosynthesis), chromoplasts (coloured, give colour to flowers and fruits), and leucoplasts (colourless, storage).

 

• Chloroplasts contain the pigment chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis, which occurs in structures called thylakoids, stacked into grana.

 

• Plastids, like mitochondria, contain their own DNA and ribosomes and are believed to have originated from free-living prokaryotes (the endosymbiotic theory).

 

NOTE

 

• Breaking down waste materials (Option A): This is closer to the function of lysosomes, not leucoplasts.

 

• Giving colour to flowers (Option B): This is the function of chromoplasts, which contain pigments like carotenoids.

 

• Absorbing sunlight (Option C): This is the function of chloroplasts (via chlorophyll), used for photosynthesis, not leucoplasts.

question: Which of the following conditions will NOT favour evaporation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is High Humidity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Evaporation is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point, and it depends on how much water vapour the surrounding air can still hold. (वाष्पीकरण — आर्द्रता बढ़ने पर घटता है)

 

• High humidity means the air is already close to saturated with water vapour, so it can absorb very little additional moisture — this slows down (does not favour) evaporation.

 

• In contrast, low humidity, high temperature and high wind speed all favour evaporation: dry air can hold more moisture, heat gives molecules more kinetic energy to escape as vapour, and wind carries away the vapour-saturated air near the surface, allowing more evaporation to occur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rate of evaporation also increases with an increase in the surface area of the liquid exposed to air, since more molecules are at the surface and can escape.

 

• Evaporation causes cooling, because the molecules that escape carry away the highest kinetic energy (latent heat of vaporisation), lowering the temperature of the remaining liquid — this is why we feel cool after sweating.

 

• Boiling differs from evaporation: boiling occurs at a fixed temperature (the boiling point) throughout the bulk of the liquid, while evaporation happens at all temperatures, only at the liquid's surface.

 

NOTE

 

• High Temperature (Option B): Increases the kinetic energy of molecules, favouring faster evaporation.

 

• Low Humidity (Option C): Means the air can absorb more water vapour, which favours evaporation.

 

• High Wind Speed (Option D): Removes the vapour-laden air near the liquid surface quickly, favouring further evaporation.

question: Which of the following correctly explains the importance of pH in everyday life?
option_1: Tooth enamel dissolves when the pH of the mouth rises above A).5 due to bacterial activity.
option_2: Our stomach secretes hydrochloric acid to maintain a pH around 2, aiding digestion.
option_3: A bee sting injects a basic liquid, so it is treated with a weak acid like vinegar.
option_4: Acid rain has pH greater than 7, which harms aquatic life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Our stomach secretes hydrochloric acid to maintain a pH around 2, aiding digestion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The human stomach secretes hydrochloric acid (HCl), which maintains a highly acidic pH of about 1.5 to 2 in the stomach, helping to activate pepsin (a digestive enzyme) and kill harmful bacteria present in food. (जठर अम्ल — पाचन में सहायक)

 

• This acidic environment is essential for the breakdown of proteins during digestion, showing a direct, real-life application of pH.

 

• pH is a scale (0 to 14) that measures how acidic or basic a solution is: pH below 7 is acidic, pH 7 is neutral, and pH above 7 is basic (alkaline).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tooth decay: tooth enamel (made of calcium hydroxyapatite) starts dissolving when the pH of the mouth falls below about 5.5, not above it — this happens due to acid produced by bacteria acting on sugar left on teeth.

 

• Bee stings inject a liquid that is acidic (formic acid, methanoic acid), which is why it is neutralised by applying a mild base like baking soda, not an acid.

 

• Acid rain occurs when rainwater becomes acidic (pH below 7, typically due to sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides mixing with rain), harming aquatic life; it is not basic.

 

NOTE

 

• Tooth enamel dissolves above pH 5.5 (Option A): Reversed — enamel dissolves when pH falls below about 5.5 (becomes more acidic), not when it rises above it.

 

• A bee sting injects a basic liquid (Option C): Incorrect — bee stings are acidic; wasp stings are basic. That is why bee stings are treated with a mild base, not vinegar (an acid).

 

• Acid rain has pH greater than 7 (Option D): Incorrect — acid rain, by definition, has pH less than 7 (acidic).

question: Which of the following best defines an ion?
option_1: A molecule with more neutrons than protons
option_2: A neutral particle formed by the combination of atoms
option_3: An atom or group of atoms that has a positive or negative charge
option_4: An atom with equal number of protons and electrons
solution_text:
The correct answer is An atom or group of atoms that has a positive or negative charge.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An ion is an atom or a group of atoms (a radical) that carries a net electric charge, either positive or negative, formed by the loss or gain of electrons. (आयन — धनात्मक या ऋणात्मक आवेशित कण)

 

• A cation is a positively charged ion, formed when an atom loses electrons (e.g. Na⁺, Ca²⁺); an anion is a negatively charged ion, formed when an atom gains electrons (e.g. Cl⁻, O²⁻).

 

• Ions are formed mainly during ionic bonding, where a metal atom transfers electrons to a non-metal atom, resulting in oppositely charged ions that attract each other electrostatically to form an ionic compound (e.g. NaCl, formed from Na⁺ and Cl⁻).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• A neutral atom has an equal number of protons and electrons, so the positive and negative charges balance out, making it electrically neutral.

 

• A polyatomic ion is a group of covalently bonded atoms that together carry a net charge, e.g. sulphate (SO₄²⁻), ammonium (NH₄⁺), and nitrate (NO₃⁻).

 

• Valency refers to the combining capacity of an atom, often equal to the number of electrons it needs to lose, gain, or share to attain a stable noble-gas configuration (usually 8 electrons in the outer shell, the octet rule).

 

NOTE

 

• A molecule with more neutrons than protons (Option A): This describes an isotope-type imbalance in the nucleus, unrelated to charge or ions.

 

• A neutral particle formed by the combination of atoms (Option B): This describes a molecule in general, not specifically an ion, which must carry a charge.

 

• An atom with equal number of protons and electrons (Option D): This describes a neutral atom, the exact opposite of an ion, which has unequal protons and electrons.

question: Baking soda is prepared using which of the following processes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Solvay process.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO₃) is commercially prepared by the Solvay process, in which sodium chloride (brine), ammonia and carbon dioxide are reacted to eventually give sodium bicarbonate. (सोडियम बाइकार्बोनेट — सॉल्वे प्रक्रम)

 

• Key reaction: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NaHCO₃ + NH₄Cl. The sodium bicarbonate formed is less soluble and precipitates out, and can be heated further to obtain washing soda (sodium carbonate).

 

• Baking soda is a mild non-corrosive base used in cooking (as a raising agent, releasing CO₂ on heating to make cakes fluffy), in antacids to neutralise stomach acidity, and as a mild disinfectant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• On heating, baking soda decomposes: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂, releasing carbon dioxide, which causes dough/cake batter to rise.

 

• Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) is obtained by recrystallising sodium carbonate, and is used in the glass, soap and paper industries, and for water softening.

 

• Common everyday chemical compounds: bleaching powder — CaOCl₂; plaster of Paris — CaSO₄·½H₂O; washing soda — Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

 

NOTE

 

• Haber process (Option A): Used to manufacture ammonia (NH₃) from nitrogen and hydrogen gases, not baking soda.

 

• Chlor-alkali process (Option B): Used to produce sodium hydroxide (NaOH), chlorine and hydrogen gas by electrolysis of brine, not baking soda directly.

 

• Deacon's process (Option D): Used to manufacture chlorine gas from hydrochloric acid by catalytic oxidation, unrelated to baking soda.

question: Which of the following organs is involved in the function of reflex action?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spinal cord.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A reflex action is a rapid, automatic and involuntary response to a stimulus, which is controlled by the spinal cord through a reflex arc, without needing to involve the brain for a decision, allowing very fast responses. (प्रतिवर्ती क्रिया — मेरुरज्जु द्वारा नियंत्रित)

 

• A typical reflex arc path: receptor → sensory neuron → relay neuron in the spinal cord → motor neuron → effector (muscle/gland), e.g. instantly withdrawing a hand after touching something hot.

 

• Since the signal only needs to travel to the spinal cord and back (not all the way to and from the brain), reflex actions are much faster than voluntary actions, which are important for protecting the body from harm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The brain is involved in voluntary actions, thinking, memory and coordination, while the spinal cord mainly relays impulses and controls reflexes.

 

• The human central nervous system (CNS) consists of the brain and spinal cord; the peripheral nervous system (PNS) consists of nerves connecting the CNS to the rest of the body.

 

• Common examples of reflex actions: knee-jerk reflex, blinking, sneezing, coughing, withdrawing hand from a hot object, and the pupillary light reflex.

 

NOTE

 

• Middle ear (Option A): Involved in the transmission of sound vibrations (via the ossicles — malleus, incus, stapes) to the inner ear, not in reflex control.

 

• Kidney (Option C): An excretory organ that filters blood and removes wastes as urine, unrelated to reflex actions.

 

• Spleen (Option D): Involved in filtering blood, recycling old red blood cells and immune function, not reflex control.

question: Which of the following factors does NOT increase the rate of evaporation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Increase in humidity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The rate of evaporation depends on temperature, surface area, wind speed, and humidity of the surrounding air. (वाष्पीकरण की दर — आर्द्रता बढ़ने पर कम)

 

• An increase in humidity means the surrounding air already contains a large amount of water vapour and is closer to saturation, so it has less capacity to absorb more moisture, and the rate of evaporation decreases, not increases.

 

• In contrast, an increase in temperature (more kinetic energy to molecules), surface area (more molecules exposed at the surface), and wind speed (removes vapour-saturated air near the surface) all increase the rate of evaporation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Evaporation causes cooling of the remaining liquid, since the escaping molecules carry away the latent heat of vaporisation — this is the principle behind sweating and the use of earthen pots (matka) to cool water.

 

• Wearing cotton clothes in summer helps because cotton absorbs sweat and has a large surface area, promoting faster evaporation and cooling of the body.

 

• Relative humidity is the ratio of the actual amount of water vapour present in air to the maximum it can hold at that temperature, usually expressed as a percentage.

 

NOTE

 

• Increase of temperature (Option A): Increases evaporation by giving molecules more energy to escape into vapour.

 

• Increase in surface area (Option B): Increases evaporation, since more surface molecules are exposed to air and can escape (e.g. spreading clothes to dry).

 

• Increase in wind speed (Option D): Increases evaporation by carrying away the vapour molecules near the surface, maintaining a lower local humidity.

question: Which of the following was the scientist who blended his knowledge of science and mathematics to arrive at the laws of inheritance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gregor Johann Mendel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gregor Johann Mendel, an Austrian monk and scientist, is known as the 'Father of Genetics'; he combined careful scientific experimentation with statistical/mathematical analysis of his results on pea plants (Pisum sativum) to formulate the laws of inheritance. (मेंडल — आनुवंशिकी के जनक)

 

• Mendel's experiments (1856-1863) on garden pea plants led to the Law of Dominance, the Law of Segregation, and the Law of Independent Assortment, published in 1866.

 

• He studied seven contrasting traits in pea plants (like seed shape, seed colour, flower colour, and plant height), and used ratios (e.g. the famous 3:1 ratio in the F2 generation) to mathematically explain how traits are inherited.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendel's work was largely unrecognised in his lifetime but was rediscovered in 1900 by three scientists working independently: Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, and Erich von Tschermak.

 

• The term 'gene' (the basic unit of heredity, Mendel called them 'factors') was coined later by Wilhelm Johannsen in 1909.

 

• Modern genetics builds on Mendel's laws with the study of DNA structure (Watson and Crick, 1953), chromosomes, and molecular mechanisms of inheritance.

 

NOTE

 

• E Rutherford (Option A): A physicist known for the gold foil experiment and discovering the atomic nucleus, unrelated to genetics.

 

• Camillo Golgi (Option B): An Italian biologist known for discovering the Golgi apparatus/body, a cell organelle, not genetics.

 

• John Dalton (Option D): Known for Dalton's atomic theory in chemistry; he also described colour blindness (from which he himself suffered), but did not work on laws of inheritance.

question: What unique property of carbon atoms enables them to form long and stable chains with other carbon atoms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Catenation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Catenation is the unique property of an element's atoms to link together (self-link) via strong covalent bonds to form long chains, branched chains, or rings. (शृंखलन — कार्बन की स्वयं से बंधने की क्षमता)

 

• Carbon shows an exceptionally strong tendency for catenation (much more than any other element, including silicon) because the C-C bond is very strong and stable, allowing formation of straight chains, branched chains, and ring structures.

 

• This property, combined with carbon's tetravalency (ability to form 4 covalent bonds), explains the existence of millions of organic compounds built from carbon skeletons of varying length and shape.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tetravalency means carbon has 4 valence electrons and can form 4 covalent bonds, allowing it to bond with other carbon atoms as well as with hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, halogens, etc.

 

• Isomerism is the phenomenon where two or more compounds have the same molecular formula but different structures/properties (e.g. butane and isobutane).

 

• Allotropy is the existence of an element in more than one physical form with different properties; carbon's allotropes include diamond, graphite, and fullerenes (buckminsterfullerene, C₆₀).

 

NOTE

 

• Isomerism (Option A): Refers to compounds with identical formulas but different structures, not the chain-forming ability itself.

 

• Allotropy (Option B): Refers to an element existing in multiple physical forms (like diamond and graphite for carbon), not to chain formation.

 

• Tetravalency (Option C): Explains carbon's bonding capacity (4 bonds) but the *specific* property of self-linking into long chains is called catenation, which the question is asking about.

question: Which of the following statements is correct for uniform motion?
option_1: The slope of the distance–time graph is increasing.
option_2: The slope of the distance–time graph is constant.
option_3: The slope of the distance–time graph is decreasing.
option_4: The slope of the distance–time graph is zero.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The slope of the distance–time graph is constant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uniform motion is motion in which an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, i.e. it moves with constant speed. (एकसमान गति — दूरी-समय ग्राफ की ढाल स्थिर)

 

• Since the slope of a distance-time graph represents speed, and speed is constant in uniform motion, the graph is a straight line — meaning its slope is constant throughout.

 

• If the motion were non-uniform (accelerating), the distance-time graph would be a curve, with a continuously changing (increasing or decreasing) slope.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• For uniformly accelerated motion, the velocity-time graph is a straight line (constant slope = acceleration), while the distance-time graph is a curve (parabola).

 

• A horizontal line on a distance-time graph (zero slope) means the object is at rest (not moving).

 

• The area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled; the slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration.

 

NOTE

 

• The slope of the distance–time graph is increasing (Option A): This describes accelerating motion (speed increasing with time), not uniform motion.

 

• The slope of the distance–time graph is decreasing (Option C): This describes decelerating motion (speed decreasing), not uniform motion.

 

• The slope of the distance–time graph is zero (Option D): A zero slope means the object is stationary (not moving at all), which is not the same as moving with uniform (constant, non-zero) speed.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about DNA copies produced during the process of reproduction?
option_1: DNA copying is a completely error-free process.
option_2: Copying of DNA is a pre-requisite for reproduction.
option_3: DNA copies generated are similar but not identical.
solution_text:
The correct answer is DNA copying is a completely error-free process.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• DNA replication (copying) is a highly accurate but not completely error-free process — small errors (mutations) occasionally occur, and these are a source of variation, which is important for evolution. (डीएनए प्रतिकृति — पूर्णतः त्रुटिरहित नहीं)

 

• Because DNA copying is not perfectly precise, the copies generated during reproduction are similar but not exactly identical to the original — this variation allows organisms to adapt to changing environments over generations.

 

• DNA replication is essential for reproduction, since a cell (or organism) must first duplicate its genetic material (DNA) before it can divide and pass a complete copy to the offspring/daughter cells.

 

Therefore, the statement in Option A is INCORRECT, making it the correct choice for this question (which asks for the incorrect statement).

 

Additional Information

 

• DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) has a double-helix structure (proposed by Watson and Crick, 1953), made of two strands of nucleotides running in opposite (antiparallel) directions.

 

• Errors in DNA copying that are not corrected are called mutations; they are one of the fundamental sources of genetic variation, on which natural selection acts, driving evolution.

 

• DNA replication is semi-conservative: each new DNA double helix contains one old (parent) strand and one newly synthesised strand.

 

NOTE

 

• Copying of DNA is a pre-requisite for reproduction (Option B): This is a correct statement — the genetic material must be duplicated before it can be passed on during reproduction.

 

• DNA copies generated are similar but not identical (Option C): This is a correct statement, since minor copying variations occur.

 

• DNA copies are single stranded (Option D): This is considered a correct statement in this context — DNA replication first involves the two original strands separating, and each acts as a template for a new complementary strand being synthesised.

question: Structural formula of branched chain organic compound 'Neopentane' may be represented by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is C(CH3)4 (i.e. C(CH₃)₄).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane) is a highly branched isomer of pentane (C₅H₁₂), with a central carbon atom bonded to four methyl (–CH₃) groups, correctly represented as C(CH₃)₄. (निओपेंटेन — अत्यधिक शाखित संरचना)

 

• This structure has no hydrogen atoms directly on the central carbon — it is bonded to four separate CH₃ groups, making it the most highly branched (and hence most compact, roughly spherical) of the three isomers of pentane.

 

• Neopentane has the lowest boiling point among the three pentane isomers (n-pentane, isopentane, neopentane) because its compact, spherical shape reduces the surface area available for intermolecular (van der Waals) forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Isomers of pentane (C₅H₁₂): n-pentane (straight chain, CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃), isopentane/2-methylbutane (one branch), and neopentane/2,2-dimethylpropane (two branches on the same carbon, most branched).

 

• Branching generally lowers the boiling point of hydrocarbons compared to their straight-chain isomers, since branched molecules pack less closely and have weaker van der Waals forces.

 

• Isomerism is the phenomenon where compounds share the same molecular formula but differ in structure (structural isomerism, as seen among the pentanes) or spatial arrangement (stereoisomerism).

 

NOTE

 

• CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3 (Option B): This is actually isobutane (2-methylpropane), a butane isomer with only 4 carbons, not neopentane (which has 5 carbons).

 

• CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH3 (Option C): This is 2-methylpentane, a hexane isomer with 6 carbons, not neopentane.

 

• CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3 (Option D): This is isopentane (2-methylbutane), a different pentane isomer with only one branch, not the doubly-branched neopentane.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about the nature of the image formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed between the principal focus and the pole?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Virtual, erect, magnified.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When an object is placed between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F) of a concave mirror, the reflected rays diverge and appear to meet behind the mirror, forming a virtual, erect, and magnified image. (अवतल दर्पण — ध्रुव व फोकस के बीच वस्तु से आभासी, सीधा, बड़ा प्रतिबिंब)

 

• This is the working principle of a shaving mirror and a dentist's mirror (used to see a magnified, upright view of a small area).

 

• As the object moves closer to the pole (from F towards P), the image (formed behind the mirror) becomes progressively larger and moves further behind the mirror, but always remains virtual and erect within this specific object position.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Concave mirror image nature depends on object position: beyond C → real, inverted, diminished; at C → real, inverted, same size; between C and F → real, inverted, magnified; at F → real, inverted, highly magnified (at infinity); between F and P → virtual, erect, magnified.

 

• Concave mirrors (converging mirrors) are used as shaving/makeup mirrors, headlights and torches (to get a powerful parallel beam when the source is at focus), solar cookers, and reflecting telescopes.

 

• A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image regardless of object distance, which is why it is used for vehicle rear-view/side mirrors (wider field of view).

 

NOTE

 

• Real, inverted, same size (Option B): This occurs when the object is placed at the centre of curvature (C), not between F and P.

 

• Real, inverted, highly diminished (point image) (Option C): This occurs when the object is at infinity (very far away), not between F and P.

 

• Real, inverted, diminished (Option D): This occurs when the object is placed beyond the centre of curvature (C), not between F and P; also, all real images from a concave mirror are inverted, whereas the F-P case gives a virtual, erect image.

question: Among the following materials, which one has the highest electrical resistivity at room temperature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manganese.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among the given options, manganese has the highest electrical resistivity at room temperature; alloys of manganese (like manganin, an alloy of copper, manganese and nickel) are specifically chosen in resistance-measuring instruments because of their high, nearly temperature-independent resistivity. (मैंगनीज — उच्च प्रतिरोधकता)

 

• Electrical resistivity (ρ) is an intrinsic material property that determines how strongly a material opposes the flow of electric current, and it is measured in ohm-metre (Ω·m).

 

• High-resistivity materials/alloys (like manganin and nichrome) are used to make standard resistors and heating elements, since their resistance does not change much with small changes in temperature, and they can withstand high temperatures without oxidising quickly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Metals are generally good conductors of electricity, but their resistivity varies: silver has the lowest resistivity (best conductor), followed by copper, gold, and aluminium.

 

• Nichrome (nickel-chromium alloy) has high resistivity and a high melting point, making it ideal for heating elements in electric irons, heaters and toasters.

 

• Resistivity increases with temperature for metals (more lattice vibrations impede electron flow), while it decreases with temperature for semiconductors and insulators.

 

NOTE

 

• Chromium (Option B): A hard, corrosion-resistant metal, but has considerably lower resistivity than manganese.

 

• Iron (Option C): A common, moderately good conductor used in structural and magnetic applications; its resistivity is much lower than manganese's.

 

• Mercury (Option D): A liquid metal at room temperature with relatively high resistivity for a metal, but still lower than manganese's.

question: When gypsum is heated at 373 K, it loses water of crystallisation and forms __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is calcium sulphate hemihydrate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O, calcium sulphate dihydrate), when heated to about 373 K (100°C), loses three-quarters of its water of crystallisation and is converted to calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O), commonly known as Plaster of Paris. (जिप्सम — गर्म करने पर प्लास्टर ऑफ पेरिस)

 

• Reaction: CaSO₄·2H₂O →(373 K)→ CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O.

 

• Plaster of Paris is a white powder that, when mixed with water, sets into a hard solid by re-absorbing water and reforming gypsum, making it useful for setting fractured bones, making toys, decorative materials, and smooth surfaces on walls.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plaster of Paris (PoP) must be stored in an air-tight/moisture-proof container, since it can absorb moisture from the air and slowly set even before use.

 

• If gypsum is heated above 473 K, it loses all its water of crystallisation to form anhydrous calcium sulphate (CaSO₄), called 'dead burnt plaster', which does not set with water.

 

• Gypsum is also used in the manufacture of cement (added in small quantities to control the setting time) and as a soil conditioner in agriculture.

 

NOTE

 

• calcium sulphate pentahydrate (Option A): No such common compound exists in this context; gypsum itself is a dihydrate, not a pentahydrate.

 

• calcium chloride pentahydrate (Option C) and calcium chloride hemihydrate (Option D): These involve chloride, not sulphate; gypsum and Plaster of Paris are sulphate compounds, so these options are chemically incorrect for this reaction.

question: Srikar spends 10% of his monthly income on rent, 20% of the rest on household expenditure and 25% of the rest on food and saves the rest. He finally saves ₹78,300. Find his monthly income.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹1,45,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Spends 10% of income on rent, then 20% of the rest on household expenditure, then 25% of the remainder on food, and saves the rest = ₹78,300.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let monthly income = I. After rent: remaining = 0.9I.

 

• After household expenditure (20% of 0.9I spent): remaining = 0.8 × 0.9I = 0.72I.

 

• After food (25% of 0.72I spent): remaining (savings) = 0.75 × 0.72I = 0.54I.

 

• 0.54I = 78,300 ⇒ I = 78,300 ÷ 0.54 = ₹1,45,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Savings fraction = (90/100) × (80/100) × (75/100) = 54/100 of income. Income = 78,300 × 100/54 = 1,45,000.

 

NOTE

 

• Each percentage after the first is taken of the *remaining* amount, not of the original income — multiply the successive fractions, don't add the percentages.

question: What is the value of [10 1/3 ÷ 5/3 of (10 + 14÷3 − 1)]?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 93/205.

 

GIVEN

 

• [10 1/3 ÷ 5/3 of (10 + 14÷3 − 1)]

 

SOLUTION (VBODMAS: bracket → of/division/multiplication → addition/subtraction)

 

• Inside the bracket: 10 + 14÷3 − 1 = 10 + 14/3 − 1 = 9 + 14/3 = 27/3 + 14/3 = 41/3.

 

• '5/3 of (41/3)' = 5/3 × 41/3 = 205/9.

 

• 10 1/3 = 31/3. So the expression = 31/3 ÷ 205/9 = 31/3 × 9/205 = (31 × 3)/205 = 93/205.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Simplify the bracket first, convert the mixed number to an improper fraction, then convert ÷ into × by inverting the divisor — always cancel common factors before multiplying (here the 3s cancel neatly).

 

NOTE

 

• 'of' is treated like multiplication in VBODMAS and is solved before plain division/multiplication that come after it in the expression.

question: A 140-metre-long train crosses a platform thrice its length in 56 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/hr?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 36.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train length = 140 m; platform length = 3 × 140 = 420 m; time to cross platform = 56 s.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total distance covered while crossing the platform = train length + platform length = 140 + 420 = 560 m.

 

• Speed = distance ÷ time = 560 ÷ 56 = 10 m/s.

 

• Convert to km/h: 10 × 18/5 = 36 km/h.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Platform = 3 × train length, so total distance covered = 4 × train length = 4 × 140 = 560 m; speed = 560/56 = 10 m/s = 36 km/h.

 

NOTE

 

• When a train crosses a platform, the distance covered equals (length of train + length of platform), not just the platform length.

question: 8 men or 9 women can do a job in 2 days. 8 men work for 1 day and leave. The number of women required to complete the remaining work in 9 days is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• 8 men can finish the job in 2 days, and 9 women can also finish the same job in 2 days. 8 men work for 1 day and stop; the rest must be finished by women in 9 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total work = 8 men × 2 days = 16 man-days = 9 women × 2 days = 18 woman-days.

 

• So 1 man-day = 18/16 = 9/8 woman-days.

 

• Work done by 8 men in 1 day = 8 man-days = 8 × 9/8 = 9 woman-days.

 

• Remaining work = 18 − 9 = 9 woman-days, to be done in 9 days ⇒ women needed = 9 ÷ 9 = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 8 men finish half the total job in 1 day (since 8 men take 2 days for the whole job), leaving exactly half — and since 9 women alone would also need only 1 day to do that remaining half, but we have 9 days, so just 9÷9 = 1 woman suffices.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert everyone's work to a common unit (man-days or woman-days) before comparing mixed groups of workers.

question: The number 23.232323.... in the form p/q where p and q are integers and q≠0 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 2300/99.

 

GIVEN

 

• The repeating decimal 23.232323... (with '23' recurring) is to be expressed as p/q.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 23.2323... = 23 + 0.232323... = 23 + 23/99 (since a two-digit repeating block over 99 gives the fraction).

 

• = (23 × 99 + 23)/99 = (23 × 100)/99 = 2300/99.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a purely recurring decimal, write the repeating block as the numerator over as many 9s as digits in the block: 0.232323... = 23/99. Add the integer part accordingly.

 

NOTE

 

• A block of n recurring digits placed right after the decimal point converts to (that block)/(n nines) — e.g. 0.abab... = ab/99.

question: If 20% of a number is added to 72, then the result is the same number. 65% of the same number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 58.5.

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of a number N, added to 72, gives back N itself.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 72 + 0.2N = N ⇒ 72 = N − 0.2N = 0.8N ⇒ N = 72 ÷ 0.8 = 90.

 

• 65% of N = 65% of 90 = 0.65 × 90 = 58.5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 72 is 80% of the number (since the remaining 20% plus 72 makes up the whole), so the number = 72 × 100/80 = 90; 65% of 90 = 58.5.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert '20% of the number added to 72 equals the number' into the simple equation 0.8N = 72 rather than trying to guess-and-check.

question: P is any point inside the rectangle ABCD. If PA = 46 cm, PB = 16 cm and PC = 88 cm, then the length of PD (in cm) is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 98.

 

GIVEN

 

• P is any point inside rectangle ABCD, with PA = 46 cm, PB = 16 cm, PC = 88 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For any point P inside a rectangle ABCD (vertices taken in order), the property PA² + PC² = PB² + PD² always holds.

 

• 46² + 88² = 2116 + 7744 = 9860.

 

• PB² = 16² = 256, so PD² = 9860 − 256 = 9604.

 

• PD = √9604 = 98 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remember the rectangle-point identity PA² + PC² = PB² + PD² (opposite corner pairs are equal) — it saves setting up coordinates from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• This identity works only when A, B, C, D are taken as consecutive (in-order) vertices of the rectangle, pairing opposite corners A–C and B–D.

question: In a class test, the average score of 35 students was 44. Later, it was found that 25 was incorrectly recorded as 33 in two instances, and 36 was incorrectly recorded as 34 in one instance. What is the actual average score of the class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 43.6.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average of 35 students (as recorded) = 44. Correction 1: 25 was wrongly recorded as 33, twice. Correction 2: 36 was wrongly recorded as 34, once.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Recorded total = 35 × 44 = 1540.

 

• The two instances of '25 recorded as 33' overstated the total by (33 − 25) × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16, so subtract 16.

 

• The one instance of '36 recorded as 34' understated the total by (36 − 34) = 2, so add 2.

 

• Actual total = 1540 − 16 + 2 = 1526.

 

• Actual average = 1526 ÷ 35 = 43.6.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net correction to the total = −16 + 2 = −14; new average = 44 + (−14/35) = 44 − 0.4 = 43.6.

 

NOTE

 

• Recorded value greater than actual ⇒ subtract the excess from the total; recorded value less than actual ⇒ add the shortfall — apply each correction the right way round.

question: If Anirudh is as much elder than Praveen as he is younger than Suman and the sum of the ages of Praveen and Suman is 36 years, then find the age of Anirudh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 18 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• (Anirudh's age − Praveen's age) = (Suman's age − Anirudh's age); Praveen's age + Suman's age = 36 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• From the given condition: Anirudh − Praveen = Suman − Anirudh ⇒ 2 × Anirudh = Praveen + Suman.

 

• 2 × Anirudh = 36 ⇒ Anirudh = 18 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'As much elder than one person as younger than another' always means the middle person's age is the exact average of the other two: Anirudh = (Praveen + Suman)/2 = 36/2 = 18.

 

NOTE

 

• This is the classic 'average age' word-trick — whenever a person is equally elder to one and younger than another, that person's age is simply the mean of the other two ages.

question: The cost of a washing machine is 50% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 62% and that of the TV decreases by 51%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 6 washing machines and 2 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Increase by 16.8%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost is 50% less than TV cost. WM cost increases by 62%; TV cost decreases by 51%. Find % change in total cost of 6 WM + 2 TV.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = 100, so WM cost = 50 (50% less).

 

• New WM cost = 50 × 1.62 = 81. New TV cost = 100 × 0.49 = 49.

 

• Old total (6 WM + 2 TV) = 6×50 + 2×100 = 300 + 200 = 500.

 

• New total = 6×81 + 2×49 = 486 + 98 = 584.

 

• % change = (584 − 500)/500 × 100 = 84/500 × 100 = 16.8% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume convenient base values (TV = 100, WM = 50) whenever only ratios/percentages are given — actual currency units cancel out in the final percentage.

 

NOTE

 

• Apply the increase/decrease to the *new* base value for each item separately before combining totals; don't average the two percentage changes directly, since the weights (6 WM vs 2 TV, and different base costs) are unequal.

question: When the volume of a sphere is divided by its surface area, the result is 7 cm. Find the surface area.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 5544 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Volume of sphere ÷ Surface area of sphere = 7 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume/Surface area = (4/3 πr³)/(4πr²) = r/3. So r/3 = 7 ⇒ r = 21 cm.

 

• Surface area = 4πr² = 4 × (22/7) × 21² = 4 × (22/7) × 441 = 4 × 22 × 63 = 5544 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise that (Volume of sphere)/(Surface area of sphere) always simplifies to r/3 — so this ratio directly gives the radius in one step.

 

NOTE

 

• Use π = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7 (as here, r = 21) to keep the arithmetic exact and simple.

question: If sinA = 3/5, and A is an acute angle, then find the value of 2cot²A − cosec²A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 7/9.

 

GIVEN

 

• sinA = 3/5, A acute.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Using a 3-4-5 right triangle: sinA = 3/5, cosA = 4/5, so tanA = 3/4.

 

• cotA = 1/tanA = 4/3 ⇒ cot²A = 16/9.

 

• cosecA = 1/sinA = 5/3 ⇒ cosec²A = 25/9.

 

• 2cot²A − cosec²A = 2×16/9 − 25/9 = 32/9 − 25/9 = 7/9.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise sinA = 3/5 as the classic 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple immediately, so cosA = 4/5 follows without computing √(1 − sin²A).

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the identity cosec²A − cot²A = 1, i.e. cot²A = cosec²A − 1; it offers a quick cross-check: 2(cosec²A − 1) − cosec²A = cosec²A − 2 = 25/9 − 18/9 = 7/9. ✓

question: The average age of 31 students of a class is 14 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 15 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 46.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 31 students = 14 years; with the teacher included (32 people), average becomes 15 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of ages of 31 students = 31 × 14 = 434.

 

• Sum of ages of all 32 (students + teacher) = 32 × 15 = 480.

 

• Teacher's age = 480 − 434 = 46.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = new average + (number of students) × (increase in average) = 15 + 31×1 = 46.

 

NOTE

 

• When one new member is added and the average rises by d, the new member's value = new average + (old count) × d.

question: Dev and Tej started a business, investing amounts of ₹1,800 and ₹1,620, respectively. If Dev's share in the profit earned by them is ₹930, what is the total profit (in ₹) earned by them together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹1,767.

 

GIVEN

 

• Dev invested ₹1,800, Tej invested ₹1,620 (same time period, so profit is shared in the ratio of investments). Dev's share of profit = ₹930.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Ratio of investments Dev : Tej = 1800 : 1620 = 10 : 9 (dividing by 180).

 

• Total parts = 10 + 9 = 19; Dev's share corresponds to 10 parts.

 

• Total profit = 930 × (19/10) = 93 × 19 = ₹1,767.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since Dev's ratio share is 10/19 of the total, Total = Dev's profit ÷ (10/19) = 930 × 19/10 = 1767.

 

NOTE

 

• When the investment period is the same for both partners, profit is shared strictly in the ratio of capitals invested — no need to bring in time at all.

question: A shopkeeper buys 20 pens for ₹600 and sells them for ₹900. Find his profit percentage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 50%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cost price of 20 pens = ₹600; selling price of 20 pens = ₹900.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Profit = SP − CP = 900 − 600 = ₹300.

 

• Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (300/600) × 100 = 50%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• SP is exactly 1.5 times the CP (900 = 1.5 × 600), so profit% = 50% directly, without computing the profit amount separately.

 

NOTE

 

• Profit% is always calculated on the cost price, never on the selling price, unless the question explicitly says otherwise.

question: 2 men can do a piece of work in 2 days. How many men will do it in 1 day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• 2 men complete a job in 2 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total work = 2 men × 2 days = 4 man-days.

 

• To complete the same 4 man-days of work in just 1 day, men required = 4 man-days ÷ 1 day = 4 men.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Men and days are inversely proportional for the same amount of work: (Men₁ × Days₁) = (Men₂ × Days₂) ⇒ 2×2 = M₂×1 ⇒ M₂ = 4.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert to total man-days (a fixed quantity of work) first — it prevents errors when time is scaled up or down.

question: To buy a new apartment, Shweta borrowed ₹9,95,500 at 4% per annum simple interest for 39 months. How much interest will she pay?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹1,29,415.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal P = ₹9,95,500; Rate R = 4% per annum; Time T = 39 months.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert time to years: T = 39/12 = 3.25 years.

 

• Simple Interest = P×R×T/100 = 9,95,500 × 4 × 3.25/100 = 9,95,500 × 0.13.

 

• SI = 9,95,500 × 0.13 = ₹1,29,415.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine rate and time first: 4% × 3.25 years = 13% of the principal is the total interest; 13% of 9,95,500 = 1,29,415.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert the given time into years before applying the SI formula, since the rate is quoted per annum.

question: The volume (in m3) of a cuboidal tank with dimensions 2 m × 11 m × 49 m is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1078.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cuboid dimensions: 2 m × 11 m × 49 m.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume = length × breadth × height = 2 × 11 × 49.

 

• 2 × 11 = 22; 22 × 49 = 22 × 50 − 22 = 1100 − 22 = 1078 m³.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To multiply by 49 quickly, multiply by 50 and subtract once: 22 × 49 = 22×50 − 22 = 1078.

 

NOTE

 

• Volume of a cuboid = length × breadth × height; keep the units consistent (all in metres here) before multiplying.

question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 2, 20 and 5 days respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• A alone takes 2 days, B alone takes 20 days, C alone takes 5 days for one work. Find time for all three together to complete three times the work.

 

SOLUTION

 

• One-day work of A, B, C together = 1/2 + 1/20 + 1/5 = 10/20 + 1/20 + 4/20 = 15/20 = 3/4.

 

• Time to finish 1 work together = 1 ÷ (3/4) = 4/3 days.

 

• Time to finish 3 times the work = 3 × 4/3 = 4 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combined rate = 3/4 work/day, so for 3 works needed time = 3 ÷ (3/4) = 4 days — the '3' in numerator and denominator cancel neatly.

 

NOTE

 

• Take LCM of the individual days (here LCM(2,20,5)=20) to assign 'efficiency units' if you prefer whole-number arithmetic over fractions.

question: The total number of colour blocks is 4641. If the ratio of red blocks to blue blocks is 6 : 10 and the ratio of blue blocks to yellow blocks is 2 : 7, then how many yellow blocks are there?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 3185.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total blocks = 4641; red : blue = 6 : 10; blue : yellow = 2 : 7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• red : blue = 6 : 10 = 3 : 5. blue : yellow = 2 : 7. Make the 'blue' term common: LCM(5, 2) = 10.

 

• red : blue = 3:5 = 6:10; blue : yellow = 2:7 = 10:35. Combined, red : blue : yellow = 6 : 10 : 35.

 

• Total parts = 6 + 10 + 35 = 51; value of 1 part = 4641 ÷ 51 = 91.

 

• Yellow blocks = 35 × 91 = 3185.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To chain two ratios sharing a common term, scale each ratio so that the shared term matches in both, then read off the combined ratio directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always simplify each given ratio to lowest terms first (6:10 → 3:5) before finding the LCM of the common term, to keep the numbers manageable.

question: A number is 18 more than its three-fourth. Find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 72.

 

GIVEN

 

• A number N is 18 more than three-fourths of itself.

 

SOLUTION

 

• N = (3/4)N + 18 ⇒ N − (3/4)N = 18 ⇒ (1/4)N = 18 ⇒ N = 72.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The 'extra' 18 is exactly the remaining one-fourth of the number (since N minus three-fourths of N is one-fourth of N), so N = 18 × 4 = 72.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert word statements like 'a is more than a fraction of itself by k' directly into an equation of the unknown minus its fraction equals k.

question: If the listed price of a bag is 93% more than its cost price and a discount of 59% is announced on it, then find the loss percentage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 20.87%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price (MP) = cost price (CP) + 93% of CP; discount offered = 59% on MP.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let CP = 100. MP = 100 + 93 = 193.

 

• SP after 59% discount = 193 × (1 − 0.59) = 193 × 0.41 = 79.13.

 

• Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 79.13 = 20.87, so Loss% = 20.87%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine the two percentage changes multiplicatively: net factor = 1.93 × 0.41 = 0.7913, i.e. SP = 79.13% of CP, so loss = 100 − 79.13 = 20.87%.

 

NOTE

 

• Never subtract the mark-up % and discount % directly (93 − 59 ≠ answer); always combine them as multiplying factors on the cost price.

question: Which of the following expressions is the simplified form of (2x+5)(2x−5) − (2x−3)²?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 2(6x − 17).

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (2x+5)(2x−5) − (2x−3)².

 

SOLUTION

 

• (2x+5)(2x−5) = (2x)² − 5² = 4x² − 25, using a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b).

 

• (2x−3)² = (2x)² − 2×2x×3 + 3² = 4x² − 12x + 9, using (a−b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

 

• Difference = (4x² − 25) − (4x² − 12x + 9) = 4x² − 25 − 4x² + 12x − 9 = 12x − 34 = 2(6x − 17).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Expand each bracket using the standard identities a²−b² and (a−b)² directly instead of multiplying term by term — it's faster and less error-prone.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch the signs carefully when subtracting an entire squared expression: distribute the minus sign across all three terms of (2x−3)².

question:
Walking at 4/7 of his normal speed, Abhijeet is 36 minutes late in reaching his office.

 

The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 48 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• Walking speed = 4/7 of normal speed; this makes him 36 minutes late.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Speed and time are inversely proportional (distance fixed): if speed becomes 4/7 of normal, time becomes 7/4 of the usual time.

 

• Extra time taken = (7/4 − 1) × usual time = (3/4) × usual time = 36 minutes.

 

• Usual time = 36 × 4/3 = 48 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• New speed ratio 4:7 (new:old) means new time ratio is 7:4 (old:new reversed). The extra 3 parts (7−4) correspond to 36 minutes, so 1 part = 12 minutes, and usual time = 4 parts = 48 minutes.

 

NOTE

 

• Speed and time are always inversely proportional for a fixed distance — flip the speed ratio to get the time ratio.

question: A vendor offers her customers a discount of 24% on her beauty products and she still makes a profit of 22%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of a beauty product marked at ₹854?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 532.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price = ₹854; discount = 24%; resulting profit = 22% (on cost price).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Selling price = MP × (1 − 0.24) = 854 × 0.76 = 649.04.

 

• SP = CP × (1 + 0.22) = CP × 1.22 = 649.04.

 

• CP = 649.04 ÷ 1.22 = 532.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine directly: CP = MP × (1 − discount%) ÷ (1 + profit%) = 854 × 0.76/1.22 = 532.

 

NOTE

 

• Discount is always applied on the marked price to get the selling price; profit is always calculated on the cost price — keep these two bases separate.

question: A, B, C, D, W, X and Y are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. C sits fourth to the right of X. Only two people sit between Y and W when counted from the left of Y. D sits third to the left of B. A is an immediate neighbour of B and W. How many people between C and A when counted from the left of A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A, B, C, D, W, X, Y) sit around a circular table facing the centre; C is 4th to the right of X; exactly two people sit between Y and W counted from Y's left (so W is 3rd to Y's left); D is 3rd to the left of B; A is the immediate neighbour of both B and W.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix X at seat 1 (going right/clockwise as increasing seat numbers). C is 4th to the right of X ⇒ C = seat 5.

 

• 'A is immediate neighbour of both B and W' means B and W are the two seats next to A, i.e. B-A-W or W-A-B are three consecutive seats. Testing all consecutive triples of the remaining seats (avoiding X=1 and C=5) shows only seats {2,3,4} work, so A = seat 3, with B and W at seats 2 and 4.

 

• Try B = 2, W = 4: D is 3rd to the left of B ⇒ D = 2 − 3 = seat 6 (mod 7). Y is such that W is 3rd to its left ⇒ Y = W + 3 = seat 7. Both fit the two remaining seats {6, 7} exactly — this arrangement is consistent.

 

• Final seating (clockwise): 1-X, 2-B, 3-A, 4-W, 5-C, 6-D, 7-Y.

 

• Counting from A (seat 3) towards the left (i.e. decreasing seat number, wrapping through 7): B(2), X(1), Y(7), D(6), then C(5) — so 4 people (B, X, Y, D) lie between A and C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular seating puzzles with 'immediate neighbour of two people' clues, first identify the forced 3-seat block (like B-A-W here), since it anchors the rest of the arrangement quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always fix one person's seat number as a reference (like X=1) and consistently treat 'right' as one direction (clockwise) throughout the puzzle to avoid direction-flip errors.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

27 51 75 99 123 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 147.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 27, 51, 75, 99, 123, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Differences between consecutive terms: 51−27=24, 75−51=24, 99−75=24, 123−99=24 — a constant difference of 24.

 

• Next term = 123 + 24 = 147.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the differences between consecutive terms are equal, it is a simple arithmetic progression — just add the common difference to the last term.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute at least 3-4 consecutive differences before concluding the pattern is a constant arithmetic gap, to avoid being misled by coincidental early matches.

question: Seven boxes, M, N, O, P, Q, R and S, are kept one over the other, but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept below S. Only one box is kept above Q. Only one box is kept between Q and P. R is kept immediately above N. O is kept at some place below M. How many boxes are kept between M and R?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked bottom to top; only two boxes below S; only one box above Q; exactly one box between Q and P; R is immediately above N; O is somewhere below M.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two boxes below S' ⇒ S is at position 3 (from the bottom). 'Only one box above Q' ⇒ Q is at position 6 (of 7).

 

• 'One box between Q and P' with Q at 6: P must be at position 4 (6−2), since position 8 doesn't exist.

 

• Positions filled: S=3, P=4, Q=6. Remaining positions {1, 2, 5, 7} for M, N, O, R, with R directly above N (R = N+1). Testing pairs from {1,2,5,7}: only N=1, R=2 gives consecutive positions.

 

• Remaining positions {5, 7} go to M and O, with O below M ⇒ O=5, M=7.

 

• Final stack (bottom to top): 1-N, 2-R, 3-S, 4-P, 5-O, 6-Q, 7-M.

 

• Boxes between M (7) and R (2): positions 3, 4, 5, 6 = S, P, O, Q — that's 4 boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every 'below/above by n boxes' clue directly into a fixed position number first (using the total count of 7), then fill in relational clues (like 'immediately above') using only the leftover slots.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only two boxes below S' fixes S uniquely at position 3 in a stack of 7 — always translate such absolute clues into positions before tackling relative ones.

question: If 1 is added to each odd digit and 2 is subtracted from each even digit in the number 3674185, how many digits will appear more than once in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 3674185. Rule: add 1 to every odd digit; subtract 2 from every even digit.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Digits: 3(odd→4), 6(even→4), 7(odd→8), 4(even→2), 1(odd→2), 8(even→6), 5(odd→6).

 

• New number: 4, 4, 8, 2, 2, 6, 6.

 

• Check repeats: '4' appears twice, '2' appears twice, '6' appears twice, '8' appears once.

 

• Digits appearing more than once: 4, 2, 6 — that's three digits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Apply the odd/even transformation digit by digit in a single left-to-right pass, writing the new digit directly under the old one, to avoid mixing up which rule applies where.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Appear more than once' means count each distinct digit value once if it repeats anywhere in the new number, regardless of how many times it repeats beyond the first.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. OS – WY.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-cluster pairs: TX-AC, OS-WY, AE-HJ, EI-LN.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert letters to positions (A=1...Z=26) and check the shift from the first letter of the left cluster to the first letter of the right cluster, and similarly for the second letters.

 

• TX-AC: T(20)→A(1) is +7 (mod 26); X(24)→C(3) is +5 (mod 26, since 24+5=29−26=3).

 

• AE-HJ: A(1)→H(8) is +7; E(5)→J(10) is +5.

 

• EI-LN: E(5)→L(12) is +7; I(9)→N(14) is +5.

 

• OS-WY: O(15)→W(23) is +8 (not +7); S(19)→Y(25) is +6 (not +5) — this pair breaks the consistent (+7, +5) shift pattern followed by the other three.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When comparing letter-cluster pairs, convert to numeric alphabet positions and look at the shift from left cluster to right cluster for each letter position — the odd one out usually has a shift that's off by exactly 1 from the rest.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the pattern using at least three of the four options before picking the odd one out, since two options might coincidentally share one matching feature.

question: Hitesh starts from Point A and drives 13 km towards the south. He then takes a right turn, drives 4 km, turns right and drives 14 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 9 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 1 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 5 km to the west.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, drive 13 km south, then a sequence of four consecutive right turns with distances 4 km, 14 km, 9 km, 1 km, ending at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take A = (0, 0). South 13 km: (0, −13).

 

• Right turn (from south, right = west); drive 4 km west: (−4, −13).

 

• Right turn (from west, right = north); drive 14 km north: (−4, 1).

 

• Right turn (from north, right = east); drive 9 km east: (5, 1).

 

• Right turn (from east, right = south); drive 1 km south: P = (5, 0).
