• Distance from P(5,0) to A(0,0) = 5 units; since P is to the east of A (x=5>0), Hitesh must travel 5 km to the west to reach A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net (x, y) displacement using compass directions (N=+y, S=−y, E=+x, W=−x); the final answer is simply the reverse direction of the net displacement vector.

 

NOTE

 

• After a right turn the facing direction always rotates 90° clockwise in the cycle North→East→South→West→North; keep this cycle fixed to avoid direction errors.

question:
Select the triad which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two triads given below. Both triads follow the same pattern.

 

WP-SL-OR

TM-PI-LO
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. QJ-MF-IL.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triad 1: WP-SL-OR. Triad 2: TM-PI-LO.

 

SOLUTION

 

• First letters of the three clusters in each triad fall by 4 each time: W(23)→S(19)→O(15), and T(20)→P(16)→L(12).

 

• Within each triad, the second letter equals (first letter − 7) for the first two clusters, and (first letter + 3) for the third cluster: e.g. W(23)−7=16=P ✓, S(19)−7=12=L ✓, O(15)+3=18=R ✓ — matching WP, SL, OR exactly; the same rule reproduces TM, PI, LO.

 

• Applying this to option B, QJ-MF-IL: first letters Q(17), M(13), I(9) fall by 4 each time ✓. Second letters: Q−7=10=J ✓ (QJ), M−7=6=F ✓ (MF), I+3=12=L ✓ (IL) — every check passes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In multi-cluster letter patterns, first find how the *first* letters of each cluster progress (here, −4 each step); once fixed, that pins down the starting letter of the answer, then verify the second-letter rule to confirm.

 

NOTE

 

• Test the derived rule against *both* given triads before applying it to the options, since a rule that fits only one triad may be coincidental.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

All goats are lions.

All lions are dogs

 

Conclusion (I): All dogs are goats.

Conclusion (II): Some lions are goats.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Only conclusion (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: All goats are lions; All lions are dogs.

 

• Conclusions: (I) All dogs are goats; (II) Some lions are goats.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'All goats are lions' means Goats is a subset of Lions; 'All lions are dogs' means Lions is a subset of Dogs. So Goats ⊆ Lions ⊆ Dogs.

 

• Conclusion I ('All dogs are goats') reverses the relation between Dogs and Goats — a universal statement cannot simply be reversed into another universal statement, so it does not follow.

 

• Conclusion II ('Some lions are goats') follows directly by conversion of 'All goats are lions' — since Goats ⊆ Lions and goats exist, at least some lions must be goats. This follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• A universal statement 'All A are B' always converts validly to the particular statement 'Some B are A' — memorise this one conversion rule to instantly resolve many syllogism conclusions.

 

NOTE

 

• Never assume 'All A are B' implies 'All B are A' — that reversal is a very common syllogism trap.

question:
In a code language,

A + B means 'A is the sister of B'

A - B means 'A is the father of B'

A x B means 'A is the mother of B'

A ÷ B means 'A is the brother of B'

Based on the above, how is P related to E if 'P - Q + C x D ÷ E'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Mother's father.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: + sister, − father, × mother, ÷ brother. Expression: P − Q + C × D ÷ E.

 

SOLUTION

 

• P − Q: P is the father of Q.

 

• Q + C: Q is the sister of C, so C is also a child of P (same parents as Q).

 

• C × D: C is the mother of D.

 

• D ÷ E: D is the brother of E, so D and E are siblings, and C (D's mother) is also E's mother.

 

• So C is E's mother, and P is C's father — therefore P is E's mother's father.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a quick family tree as you decode each symbol left to right, marking generations clearly (P above Q/C, C above D/E) — it prevents confusion in multi-step blood relation codes.

 

NOTE

 

• 'A + B' (A is sister of B) implies A and B share the same parents; use this to correctly place C in the same generation as Q under P.

question: Naksh ranked 45th from the top and 27th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 71.

 

GIVEN

 

• Naksh's rank = 45th from the top; 27th from the bottom.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total students = (rank from top) + (rank from bottom) − 1, since Naksh himself is counted in both ranks.

 

• Total = 45 + 27 − 1 = 71.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Total = top rank + bottom rank − 1; the '−1' always accounts for not double-counting the person himself.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is forgetting to subtract 1, which would incorrectly give 72 instead of 71.

question:
A group of numbers/symbols is coded using letter codes as per the codes given below and the conditions that follow. The correct combination of codes following the conditions is your answer.

Note: If none of the conditions apply, then the codes for the respective number/symbol are to be followed directly as given in the table.

 

Numbers/symbols: %  6  2  8  *  3  &  7  @  9  +  5  #  4

Codes:           T  W  P  H  G  L  F  U  M  B  S  Y  K  D

 

Conditions:

(i) If the first element is a symbol and the last element is a number, the codes for these two (first and last elements) are to be interchanged.

(ii) If both the second and third elements are symbols, the code for the third is to be coded as the code for the second element.

(iii) If the first element is a symbol and the fourth element is an odd number, the first and fourth elements are to be coded as ©.

 

What will be the code for the following group?

% 5 * & 9
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. B Y G F T.

 

GIVEN

 

• Group: % 5 * & 9. Base codes from the table: % = T, 5 = Y, * = G, & = F, 9 = B.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Base codes in order: T, Y, G, F, B (for %, 5, *, &, 9).

 

• Check condition (i): first element (%) is a symbol, last element (9) is a number ⇒ interchange the codes of the first and last elements. First becomes B, last becomes T.

 

• Check condition (ii): second element (5) is a number, not a symbol, so this condition does not apply.

 

• Check condition (iii): fourth element (&) is a symbol, not an odd number, so this condition does not apply.

 

• Final codes: position1=B, position2=Y, position3=G, position4=F, position5=T → B Y G F T.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write the plain (uncoded) sequence of codes first from the table, then apply the numbered conditions one at a time, in order, only modifying the positions each condition specifically addresses.

 

NOTE

 

• A condition applies only when *every* part of its stated requirement is satisfied (e.g. condition (iii) needs both 'first is a symbol' AND 'fourth is an odd number') — check each part separately before applying it.

question: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. HJ - DL.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-cluster pairs: NO-JK, LM-HI, HJ-DL, QR-MN.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check each pair: both letters in the left cluster and both letters in the right cluster should be consecutive alphabet letters, with a fixed shift of −4 from left cluster to right cluster.

 

• NO-JK: N,O consecutive (gap 1); J,K consecutive (gap 1); N→J is −4. ✓

 

• LM-HI: L,M consecutive; H,I consecutive; L→H is −4. ✓

 

• QR-MN: Q,R consecutive; M,N consecutive; Q→M is −4. ✓

 

• HJ-DL: H,J have a gap of 2 (not consecutive); D,L have a gap of 8 (not consecutive) — this pair does not follow the 'consecutive letters' pattern of the other three.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When checking letter-cluster groups, quickly note the internal gap between the two letters of each cluster (e.g. consecutive = gap of 1) — the odd one out often has a mismatched internal gap.

 

NOTE

 

• Confirm the pattern using the internal gap of *both* clusters in a pair, not just one, since HJ-DL fails on both counts here.

question:
Select the pair which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two pairs given below. Both pairs follow the same pattern.

 

GHI-FGH

KLM-JKL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. BCD-ABC.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets:

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

 

(12, 240, 20)

(10, 150, 15)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. (9, 180, 20).

 

GIVEN

 

• Sets: (12, 240, 20) and (10, 150, 15).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the relation between the first and third numbers, multiplied together, against the middle number: 12 × 20 = 240 ✓ (matches the middle number). 10 × 15 = 150 ✓ (matches the middle number).

 

• So the rule is: (first number) × (third number) = (middle number).

 

• Testing option B (9, 180, 20): 9 × 20 = 180 ✓ — matches perfectly.

 

• Testing the others: (8,100,15): 8×15=120≠100. (15,225,16): 15×16=240≠225. (8,90,15): 8×15=120≠90 — none of these work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With three numbers in a set, first test the simplest possible relation — product of the outer two numbers equalling the middle one — before trying more complex operations.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly disallows digit-breaking tricks, so always test whole-number operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) on the numbers as given.

question: A, B, C, E, F, P, and Q are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. Only four people sit between C and E, when counted from the right of C. C sits third to the left of P. B sits third to the left of F. Q is an immediate neighbour of both E and P. How many people between A and Q, when counted from the right of A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A, B, C, E, F, P, Q) around a circular table facing centre; four people between C and E counted from C's right; C is 3rd to the left of P; B is 3rd to the left of F; Q is the immediate neighbour of both E and P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix C at seat 1 (clockwise = right, increasing seat numbers). 'Four people between C and E from C's right' means E is 5th from C ⇒ E = seat 6.

 

• 'C is 3rd to the left of P' ⇒ P = C + 3 = seat 4.

 

• 'Q is immediate neighbour of both E and P' means E and P are Q's two neighbours, so E-Q-P (or P-Q-E) must be consecutive. Since P=4 and E=6, Q must sit at seat 5 (between them).

 

• Remaining seats {2, 3, 7} for A, B, F, with B 3rd to the left of F (F = B + 3). Testing B=7: F = 7+3 = 3 (mod 7) — fits the remaining seats.

 

• Remaining seat 2 goes to A.

 

• Final seating (clockwise): 1-C, 2-A, 3-F, 4-P, 5-Q, 6-E, 7-B.

 

• Counting from A (seat 2) to the right: 3-F, 4-P, then reach 5-Q — so 2 people (F, P) lie between A and Q.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Immediate neighbour of both X and Y' always forces X and Y to sit exactly two seats apart with the subject sandwiched between them — locate this triple first before placing the rest.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep a single consistent 'right = clockwise, increasing seat number' convention throughout to avoid sign errors when converting clues into seat numbers.

question:
Refer to the number series given below and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only.

(NOTE: All numbers are single-digit numbers only.)

 

(Left) 5 2 4 8 8 7 2 3 3 3 6 7 5 6 6 8 9 4 1 5 1 7 7 3 3 7 5 (Right)

 

How many such odd numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an even number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sequence: 5 2 4 8 8 7 2 3 3 3 6 7 5 6 6 8 9 4 1 5 1 7 7 3 3 7 5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Mark each digit O (odd) or E (even), left to right: O E E E E O E O O O E O O E E E O E O O O O O O O O O.

 

• A qualifying number is an odd digit whose immediate left AND immediate right neighbours are both even.

 

• Scanning the sequence: the digit '7' at position 6 has neighbours 8(E) and 2(E) — qualifies.

 

• The digit '9' (17th position) has neighbours 8(E) and 4(E) — qualifies.

 

• No other odd digit in the sequence has even digits on both sides.

 

• Total qualifying odd numbers = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert the whole sequence into a string of O/E letters first; then simply scan for the exact 3-letter pattern 'E O E' — each match is one qualifying number.

 

NOTE

 

• The very first and last digits of the sequence can never qualify, since they are missing one neighbour — skip them when scanning.

question:

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

 

TIU 20  VKW 21  XMY 22  ZOA 23  ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. BQC 24.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: TIU 20, VKW 21, XMY 22, ZOA 23, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• First letters: T(20), V(22), X(24), Z(26) — increase by 2 each time; next = Z+2 = 28 → wraps to 28−26 = 2 = B.

 

• Second letters: I(9), K(11), M(13), O(15) — increase by 2 each time; next = O+2 = 17 = Q.

 

• Third letters: U(21), W(23), Y(25), A(1, wrapping from 25+2=27−26=1) — increase by 2 each time (with wraparound); next = A+2 = 3 = C.

 

• Attached numbers: 20, 21, 22, 23 — increase by 1 each time; next = 24.

 

• Combining: BQC 24.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split letter-number clusters into separate independent tracks (letter 1, letter 2, letter 3, number) and find each track's step size on its own — here all three letter tracks share the same +2 step, just starting at different letters.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the alphabet wraps after Z back to A (26 → 1); this is needed to correctly get the third letter here (Y → A).

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements: Some hair are nails. All nails are teeth.

 

Conclusions (I): Some hair are teeth.

Conclusions (II): All teeth are nails.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: Some hair are nails; All nails are teeth.

 

• Conclusions: (I) Some hair are teeth; (II) All teeth are nails.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Some hair are nails' + 'All nails are teeth' combine validly (Some-All chaining) to give: Some hair are teeth. Conclusion I follows.

 

• 'All nails are teeth' cannot be reversed into 'All teeth are nails' — a universal statement doesn't imply its converse as a universal statement. Conclusion II does not follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The chain 'Some A are B' + 'All B are C' always validly gives 'Some A are C' — memorise this standard syllogism combination.

 

NOTE

 

• 'All B are C' only converts validly to 'Some C are B', never to 'All C are B' — don't fall for the reversed universal statement trap.

question:

GIVEN

question: If 1 is added to each odd digit and 2 is subtracted from each even digit in the number 6437585, how many digits will appear more than once in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 6437585. Rule: add 1 to odd digits; subtract 2 from even digits.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Digits: 6(even→4), 4(even→2), 3(odd→4), 7(odd→8), 5(odd→6), 8(even→6), 5(odd→6).

 

• New number: 4, 2, 4, 8, 6, 6, 6.

 

• Check repeats: '4' appears twice (1st, 3rd positions); '6' appears three times (5th, 6th, 7th positions); '2' and '8' appear once each.

 

• Digits appearing more than once: 4 and 6 — that's two distinct digits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Do the digit transformation in one clean left-to-right pass, then simply tally frequency of each resulting digit (0-9) to spot repeats quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• The question asks how many *distinct digits* repeat, not how many total repeated occurrences there are — count 6 (which repeats 3 times) as just one qualifying digit, not two or three.

How many such odd numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

11 13 16 21 ? 39
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 28.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 11, 13, 16, 21, ?, 39.

 

SOLUTION

• Missing term = 21 + 7 = 28.

question: Five people, A, B, C, D and E, are sitting in a row, facing north. Only two people sit between A and B. B sits second to the left of E. Who sits at the extreme left end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. B.

 

GIVEN

 

• 5 people A, B, C, D, E in a row facing north; exactly two people sit between A and B; B sits second to the left of E.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'B sits second to the left of E' ⇒ B = E − 2. Testing E = 3: B = 1.

 

• 'Only two people sit between A and B' ⇒ A is 3 seats away from B. With B = 1, A = 1 + 3 = seat 4 (seat −2 is invalid).

 

• Positions so far: B = 1, E = 3, A = 4. The remaining seats {2, 5} go to C and D (in either order), which does not affect who occupies the extreme ends.

 

• Final row (left to right): B(1), [C/D](2), E(3), A(4), [D/C](5).

 

• The extreme left seat (position 1) is occupied by B.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In row-arrangement puzzles, convert 'x sits second to the left of y' directly to x = y − 2, and 'n people between p and q' to |position(p) − position(q)| = n + 1 — this quickly narrows down valid seat numbers.

 

NOTE

 

• When two people's relative order (like C and D here) isn't pinned down by any clue, they can be swapped freely — only report what the clues definitely fix, such as the extreme-left seat here.

question: In a certain code language, 'MOVE' is coded as '7481' and 'OVER' is coded as '8314'. What is the code for 'R' in that language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• MOVE → 7481; OVER → 8314.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Letters M, O, V, E are common to the word 'MOVE'; letters O, V, E, R are common to 'OVER'. Notice the letter M appears only in MOVE, and the letter R appears only in OVER.

 

• Similarly, among the digits, '7' appears in MOVE's code (7481) but not in OVER's code (8314); the digits 8, 3, 1, 4 are shared/rearranged between both codes.

 

• Since M is the only letter unique to MOVE, and 7 is the only digit unique to MOVE's code, M is coded as 7.

 

• By the same logic, R is the only letter unique to OVER, and 3 is the only digit unique to OVER's code — so R is coded as 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two coded words share three of four letters, the digit that appears in only one word's code must correspond to that word's one unique letter — a fast way to crack partial-overlap coding questions.

 

NOTE

 

• This method identifies only the uniquely-placed letters (M and R here) confidently; the shared letters (O, V, E) cannot be individually pinned down from this data alone, but that isn't needed to answer the question asked.

question: Each of the digits in the number 9612345 is arranged in ascending order from left to right. What will be the sum of the digits that are second from the left and second from the right in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 8.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 9612345.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Digits: 9, 6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Arranging in ascending order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9.

 

• Second digit from the left = 2.

 

• Second digit from the right = 6 (the number is 1-2-3-4-5-6-9, so counting from the right: 9 is 1st, 6 is 2nd).

 

• Sum = 2 + 6 = 8.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once digits are sorted, 'second from left' and 'second from right' are simply the 2nd and (n−1)th digits of the sorted sequence — read them off directly without recounting from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• Sort all digits carefully first (repeated digits, if any, must all be included) before picking out positions — a sorting mistake at this stage cascades into a wrong final answer.

question:
Arman starts from point A and drives 44 km towards south. He then takes a left turn, drives 42 km, turns left and drives 51 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 56 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 7 km and stops at point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach point A again?

(Note: All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 14 km to the east.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, drive 44 km south, then four consecutive left turns with distances 42 km, 51 km, 56 km, 7 km, ending at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take A = (0, 0). South 44 km: (0, −44).

 

• Left turn (from south, left = east); drive 42 km east: (42, −44).

 

• Left turn (from east, left = north); drive 51 km north: (42, 7).

 

• Left turn (from north, left = west); drive 56 km west: (42−56, 7) = (−14, 7).

 

• Left turn (from west, left = south); drive 7 km south: P = (−14, 0).

 

• Distance from P(−14, 0) to A(0, 0) = 14 units; since P is to the west of A (x = −14), Arman must travel 14 km to the east to reach A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track net (x, y) displacement using compass directions throughout, exactly as in a coordinate-geometry problem — the final leg's direction is simply the reverse of the net displacement vector.

 

NOTE

 

• After a left turn, the facing direction rotates 90° anticlockwise in the cycle North→West→South→East→North — keep this cycle fixed to avoid direction mix-ups.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only) Counting to be done from left to right only.

 

(Left) 4 3 5 2 9 7 2 8 7 2 1 8 7 4 5 5 2 3 5 5 6 9 6 3 3 (Right)

 

How many such odd numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sequence: 4 3 5 2 9 7 2 8 7 2 1 8 7 4 5 5 2 3 5 5 6 9 6 3 3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Mark each digit O (odd) or E (even): E O O E O O E E O E O E O E O O E O O O E O E O O.

 

• Look for odd digits with an odd digit on both sides. Most odd digits here occur singly or in pairs (both edge digits, so they fail), except one run of three consecutive odd digits: 5-5-5 at positions 18-19-20 (values 3,5,5 — let's recheck: the run is 3,5,5 at positions 18,19,20).

 

• Within this run of 3 consecutive odd digits (3, 5, 5), only the middle digit (the second 5, value at position 19) has an odd digit on both sides.

 

• No other odd digit anywhere else in the sequence has both neighbours odd — all other odd digits are either isolated (both neighbours even) or sit at the edge of a 2-digit odd run.

 

• Total qualifying odd numbers = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert to an O/E string and scan for 'O O O' triplets; count only the middle position of each such triplet — here just one such triplet exists.

 

NOTE

 

• Runs of exactly 2 consecutive odd digits never produce a qualifying number, since both digits in a 2-run sit at an edge of that run — only runs of 3 or more odd digits contribute.

MOS-QSW

solution_text:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For cluster-pair patterns, test the shift on just the first letter pair, then quickly confirm the *same* shift applies to the remaining letters — a genuine pattern will hold consistently across all three letters.

• Remember to wrap around after Z back to A (26+1→1) when checking shifts near the end of the alphabet, as needed for X→B in the second given pair.

Additional Information

• The GenomeIndia project draws samples from various population groups across India's states, aiming to represent the country's vast genetic diversity.

 

• India's biotechnology and genomics push aligns with the broader National Biotechnology Development Strategy, supporting advances in healthcare, agriculture, and personalised medicine.

 

NOTE

 

• 11,000 (Option A), 6600 (Option B), 8000 (Option C): These figures do not match the officially reported milestone; the confirmed figure as of 30 April 2025 was approximately 10,000 individuals.

question: Which of the following countries hosted the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in April 2025?

• BIMSTEC is a regional grouping comprising seven member states: India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand, formed to promote regional connectivity and cooperation across South and South-East Asia.

 

• The organisation was established in 1997 (originally as BIST-EC with four members, later expanded and renamed BIMSTEC) and its headquarters (Secretariat) is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

• India hosted the BIMSTEC Summit in 2018 (the 4th summit), held in Kathmandu, Nepal in 2018 actually — summits have rotated among member states over the years.

question: Which spacecraft will be used for Axiom-4?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crew Dragon C213.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Axiom-4 (Ax-4), a private crewed mission to the International Space Station (ISS), used the SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft (capsule C213) for transporting its crew to and from orbit. (एक्सिओम-4 मिशन — स्पेसएक्स क्रू ड्रैगन अंतरिक्ष यान)

 

• The mission was significant for India, as Indian Air Force Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla was part of the Axiom-4 crew, becoming only the second Indian to travel to space, after Rakesh Sharma's historic 1984 flight aboard a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft.

 

• Axiom Space, a private American company, organises commercial astronaut missions to the ISS in partnership with NASA and SpaceX, using the Crew Dragon capsule launched on a Falcon 9 rocket.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• SpaceX's Crew Dragon is a reusable capsule certified by NASA for crewed missions to the ISS, part of NASA's Commercial Crew Program.

 

• Rakesh Sharma flew to space in 1984 aboard Soyuz T-11, spending about 8 days on the Soviet Salyut 7 space station, and remains India's first astronaut.

 

• India's own human spaceflight programme, Gaganyaan, aims to launch Indian astronauts on an indigenously built spacecraft, independent of foreign vehicles like Crew Dragon.

 

NOTE

 

• Starliner (Option B): Boeing's crew capsule, also part of NASA's Commercial Crew Program, but not used for Axiom-4.

 

• Orion (Option C): NASA's deep-space crew capsule, used for Artemis lunar missions, not for ISS commercial trips like Axiom-4.

 

• Soyuz MS-24 (Option D): A Russian spacecraft used for separate Roscosmos-led ISS missions, unrelated to the Axiom-4 mission.

question: As per Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, the percentage of population using an improved drinking water source in rural areas increased from 94.57% in 2015-16 to what percentage in 2024-25, indicating significant progress toward universal safe water access in rural India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 96.62%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, the percentage of India's rural population using an improved drinking water source rose from 94.57% in 2015-16 to 96.62% in 2024-25, reflecting steady progress towards universal safe water access. (ग्रामीण भारत में सुरक्षित पेयजल स्रोत की उपलब्धता — 96.62%)

 

• This improvement is closely linked to the success of the Jal Jeevan Mission, launched in 2019, which aims to provide Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) to every rural household in India ('Har Ghar Jal').

 

• The National Indicator Framework (NIF), maintained by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), tracks India's progress against the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with SDG 6 focused on 'Clean Water and Sanitation'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide potable tap water supply to all rural households in India, significantly reducing the burden of manual water collection, especially for women and girls.

 

• India's SDG progress is periodically reviewed via NITI Aayog's SDG India Index, which ranks states and union territories on their progress across all 17 SDGs.

 

• SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) aims to ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all by 2030.

 

NOTE

 

• 98% (Option A), 96% (Option C), 32% (Option D — i.e. a garbled reading of a different figure): These do not match the officially reported 2024-25 figure; the confirmed progress figure in the SDG NIF Progress Report 2025 was specifically 96.62%.
